blind_target.title: A direct and conceptual replication of post-loss speeding when gambling.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Across experi-
ments, we could again replicate the finding by Langer and Roth (1975) in an online ex-
perimental setting (see also our replication study). Thus, introducing a start response
did not alter the illusion-of-control effect. Moreover, we replicated the finding that par-
ticipants speed up after losses compared to wins (Eben et al., 2020; Verbruggen et al.,
2017).

prior_decision.quote:
Across experi-

prior_decision.reason: Both experiments explicitly re-test and successfully replicate the post-loss speeding effect using the start-response procedure and exclusion criteria of Eben et al. (2020). Under the replication-chain rule, Eben et al. (2020) is the nearest target in the chain re-testing Verbruggen et al. (2017) and is an omitted target in the shipped dataset.

luna_triage.reason: The source reports post-loss speeding versus wins and attributes the finding to Eben et al. (2020) and Verbruggen et al. (2017); reference identity confirms Eben as a preceding replication in this chain. Supplied Langer and Roth (1975) is a different finding. The prior Argon objection identifies Eben as nearest target; inspection supports it.
